title: Modules of finite presentation are quasi-coherent; a quasi-coherent module is of finite type (finite presentation) on an affine open iff its sections there are a finite (finitely presented) module (Stacks 01BO, 01PB, 01PC)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. (0) Every $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation (defined below) is quasi-coherent. Now let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Then (a) $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] if and only if $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module; (b) $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation if and only if $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely presented $R$-module. Consequently (c) if $X=\bigcup_jU_j$ is an affine open covering with $\mathcal F(U_j)$ finitely generated over $\mathcal O_X(U_j)$ for all $j$, then $\mathcal F$ is of finite type and $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module for every affine open $U\subseteq X$; and if $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation then $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module for every affine open $U$.
